clue.text: Adult female has messed about with speed

indicators.note: to mess about with something is to jumble it, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the last word of the letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A woman has been fiddling with something involving speed, perhaps a car or a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'has' does double duty in the surface but in the parse it is the last word of the fodder: ADULT FEMALE HAS rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Going full steam ahead means proceeding at maximum power, an idiom from steam engines for doing something fast.

clue.text: Meal deal might be used by him, if served up with drink shortly beforehand

indicators.note: the drink comes in front of the next piece
in a down clue, served up means turned upwards, so the word is read bottom to top
said of a word, shortly means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a shandy is beer mixed with lemonade

parts.words: deal might be used by him
parts.note: Chips is the traditional nickname for a carpenter, who works deal, a kind of softwood timber

explanation.surface: A meal deal offered to a customer who takes it with a drink first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meal deal' looks like one phrase, but 'Meal' alone is the definition; 'deal' is timber, and Chips is the nickname for a carpenter in British usage. A shandy is beer with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and chips is a classic British takeaway dinner of battered fish with fried potatoes.

clue.text: Sponge John having picked up a bit of fluff

parts.note: a john is slang for a lavatory, as is loo

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so these letters are read upwards
a bit of the word fluff is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A man called John picks some fluff off a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name but is slang for a lavatory. 'picked up' turns the A and the F upwards to give FA.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah, also spelt loofa, is a dried gourd used as a bath scrubber, a type of natural sponge.

clue.text: One who follows somebody on Radio Four, ultimately

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a somebody is a person who has made it, a success

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: Someone who follows a celebrity who appears on BBC Radio Four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radio Four' is a BBC station, but here it only supplies its two final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is the person who comes next in a post or role, taking over after another.

clue.text: Service breaks in general essentially all together

indicators.note: the service forces its way into the letters taken from general
the essence of general is the run held within it, so its outer letters G and RAL are dropped

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, a church service breaks up when everyone is together.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping GENERAL down to its core leaves ENE, and MASS is pushed into its middle, giving EN-MASS-E.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French borrowed into English for in a body or as a group, everyone at once.

clue.text: Masculine types work for wimp

parts.note: M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine
ilks are kinds or types
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Macho types do the work of a weakling.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is short for opus, Latin for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, timid man, literally bread soaked in milk, so a soft, spineless sort.

clue.text: Commotion in area south of back-to-back houses

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece below comes after

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house; two of them back to back read HO then OH

explanation.surface: A disturbance in a district below some terraced back-to-back houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Back-to-backs are a style of British terraced housing, but here two HOs are set back to back, the second reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a fuss or noisy commotion, an informal word for a disturbance or uproar.

clue.text: Unreasonable dunce would be this

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a dunce is somewhat stupid

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for going too far; read literally it means rather dim.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit thick is an idiom for unfair or too much, and literally describes someone slightly stupid.

clue.text: Way to bitch regularly — not if this

definitions.note: you would not bitch if you were the answer: a stoic endures without complaint

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here of 'to bitch'

explanation.surface: A way of complaining at regular intervals, unless you happen to be a calm sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads back over the clue: someone who would not bitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic bears pain or hardship without complaining, so would never moan or gripe.

clue.text: Stage name of chairman carrying large first book?

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so Mao contains the other letters

parts.note: Chairman Mao led communist China
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
Vol I, volume one, is the first book of a set

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about the stage name a chairman uses, carrying a big first book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage name' is not a pseudonym but a name of a character on the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Malvolio is the pompous steward in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, a character name heard in the theatre.

clue.text: Through these you can see jockey ride lions — wow!

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre and shift about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A view from which you watch a jockey riding lions, to great amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel windows are projecting bay windows on upper floors, panes of glass you look out of.

clue.text: Film literally produced down under

indicators.note: literally means take 'produced down under' at its word: made inside Australia

parts.note: Down Under is Australia, abbreviated AUS
produced means made

explanation.surface: A movie that was actually shot in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: MADE is put inside AUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadeus is the 1984 Milos Forman movie about Mozart, a Best Picture Oscar winner.

clue.text: Proverbial madman on tail of nervous wreck

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means coming after
the tail of a word is its final letter

parts.note: as mad as a hatter is the proverb

explanation.surface: A mad person following a highly anxious person who has had a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous wreck' looks like a single phrase, but the definition is just 'wreck'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter something is to smash it into pieces, so ruin or destroy it completely.

clue.text: Simpson breaking bugger's back where fights occur

indicators.note: OJ breaks into the reversed letters
back means read in reverse

parts.note: sod is a British swearword, a bugger
OJ Simpson, the American footballer

explanation.surface: O.J. Simpson breaking someone's back in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bugger' and 'sod' are both British insults.
explanation.definitionFit: A dojo is a training hall for martial arts such as judo or karate, where people spar.

clue.text: Current example in New Street covered by press

indicators.note: covered by means held within another word

parts.note: to jam is to press or squeeze

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the word's letters are recast

explanation.surface: A present-day example on New Street reported in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: STREET rearranges to ETSTRE, which sits inside JAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet stream is a fast, narrow air flow high in the atmosphere, one kind of current.

clue.text: Blast, say, dynamite left by sailor around vacated emplacement

indicators.note: what is left goes around the next piece
left by means abandoned, so the sailor departs

parts.note: dynamite is an explosive
OS is Ordinary Seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, keeping only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An explosion, perhaps, as dynamite is left by a sailor near a gun position.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OS leaves EXPLIVE; ET from emplacement goes inside. 'Blast' is the defining example: a mild curse.
explanation.definitionFit: An expletive is an oath or swearword, and blast is a mild example of an exclamation like that.

clue.text: Get rid of character abroad, caught by international venture being withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign character
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to dare is to venture

explanation.surface: Remove a foreign person caught in some international enterprise that has been pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: ETACIDARE is built in order and then read backwards in full.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy something completely, uprooting it so that it is wiped out.

clue.text: Unpredictable state — storm is brewing

parts.note: HI is the postal abbreviation for Hawaii, a US state

indicators.note: brewing means stirring up, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A state where weather can't be forecast, with a storm brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit-or-miss describes something haphazard or random, sometimes succeeding and sometimes failing.

clue.text: Old tax office work finally getting a little tedious

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, Britain's former tax authority

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: some means a little or a certain amount

explanation.surface: Work at the old tax office proved rather dull in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue merged into HMRC in 2005, hence 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Irksome means annoying or tiresome, so something tedious that irritates through dullness.

clue.text: One refusing to buy anything

parts.note: buy is slang for accept or believe, so this is a person who believes nothing

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a reluctant shopper, but to buy something is also to believe it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic doubts claims and won't accept anything without evidence, a habitual doubter.

clue.text: Bent solver caught by question

indicators.note: by means alongside, next in line

parts.note: to question is to ask

indicators.note: caught means heard, so the solver word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the solver is you, the person reading the clue

explanation.surface: A twisted puzzle-solver is being interrogated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you' said aloud gives EW, the sound of a ewe.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew means crooked or not straight, so the same as bent or awry.

clue.text: Cherished getting nonsense on tap

parts.note: pet means favourite or cherished
cock is British slang for nonsense, as in cock and bull

explanation.surface: A favourite gets nonsense on demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tap' looks like a phrase, but 'on' is the link and 'tap' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A petcock is a small valve for draining pipes or engines, a kind of little spigot.

clue.text: Mathematician once picked up in tanker

indicators.note: picked up means heard by ear, so the name is taken as it sounds

parts.note: Leonhard Euler was an 18th-century Swiss mathematician, hence 'once'

explanation.surface: A mathematician from the past was found in an oil ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Euler's name is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a ship that carries oil, especially one refuelling naval vessels, a tanker.

clue.text: Rabble-rousing shunning leader in newspaper issue

indicators.note: shunning its leader means the first letter is avoided

parts.note: sedition is speech stirring people against authority

explanation.surface: A press release free of rabble-rousing content.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one print run of a newspaper, the copies issued at one time.

clue.text: Starts to interrupt reporter, asking questions in a form of Arabic

indicators.note: the starts of these words are their initial letters

explanation.surface: Someone starts to interrupt a journalist asking questions in Arabic.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraqi Arabic is the spoken dialect of Iraq, a regional variety of the language.

clue.text: Yacht leak to be fixed

indicators.note: fixed means repaired, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A yacht's leak needs mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is part of the fodder rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A keelboat is a sailing boat with a fixed keel, a kind of yacht.

clue.text: Way to work on sadly curtailed mission

indicators.note: in an across clue, the piece placed on comes after
curtailed means its tail is cut off

parts.note: alas is an exclamation said sadly
MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A way of working on a mission that, sadly, got cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the last letter from ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was a Spanish mission in Texas, famous for its siege in 1836.

clue.text: Deviant sex in cemetery introducing good ways to escape

indicators.note: introducing means bringing it into the anagram
deviant means straying from normal, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Kinky sex in a graveyard, giving good reasons to run.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency exits are doors used to get out of a building in a fire or crisis.
